{#- One nav entry and, recursively, everything beneath it. The stock theme draws two levels and stops. This override renders any depth, keeping the stock classes and the navigation.side.indexes behaviour at every level: a child page titled "Index" turns its section's header into a link to it, and gets no row of its own. -#} {%- set features = config.theme.features or [] -%} {%- import 'macros/side-nav/side-nav-item-class.j2' as class_helper with context -%} {%- import 'macros/side-nav/side-nav-item.j2' as item_helper with context -%} {%- import 'macros/side-nav/section-index-page-title.j2' as index_helper with context -%} {%- macro nav_entry(nav_item) -%} {%- if nav_item.children -%} {%- set index_matches = (nav_item.children | selectattr("title", "eq", index_helper.get_section_index_page_title()) | list) if "navigation.side.indexes" in features else [] -%} {%- set index_child = index_matches[0] if index_matches else none -%} {%- if index_child -%} {{ item_helper.index_item(index_child, class_helper.get_class(index_child)) }} {%- else -%} {{ item_helper.non_index_item(nav_item, class_helper.get_class(nav_item)) }} {%- endif %}
    {%- for child in nav_item.children if child is not sameas index_child %}
  • {{ nav_entry(child) }}
    • {%- endfor %}
{%- else -%} {{ item_helper.non_index_item(nav_item, class_helper.get_class(nav_item)) }} {%- endif -%} {%- endmacro -%}
  • {{ nav_entry(nav_item) }}
